text:
We waited 13 years for GTA 6.

We quit after 2 hours.

My brother and I had everything ready. Beer in the fridge. Pizza on the table. Phones off. When the download hit 100% at midnight, we screamed like kids.

By 2 AM the room was dead silent.

Here’s what nobody on YouTube will tell you 👇

The first hour isn’t a game. It’s a movie you hold a controller for. Cutscene. Walk. Cutscene. Drive. Cutscene. My brother asked “when does it start?” three times. It never did.

Then the game finally let us drive. 30 FPS. No 60 FPS mode. Not even on the PS5 Pro. Every fast turn looks like a smeared painting.

The stuff you only know if you’ve played it:

→ The weapon wheel is broken. In my first shootout I pulled out a flashlight instead of a shotgun
→ Jason has no personality. Half his lines are “yeah, sure, that’s fine”
→ You can get eaten by an alligator in the swamps. Honestly the most exciting thing that happened to us
→ Steal a car with a cat in the back and Jason throws it out the window. That’s the “storytelling”
→ You can ride a jet ski with your dog. Cute. Also the best part of our night
→ Grill burgers? Yes. Mini golf? Yes. Rob a bank? Not for hours
→ Most restaurants on Ocean Drive are locked. You just walk past the doors
→ Touch a kerb at speed and your car flips like it’s made of paper

What everyone wants to know:

→ Is it beautiful? Yes. Best-looking city ever made
→ Is it fun? No. Not in the first hours
→ Is it worth $70 on launch night? Not for us

It feels like more money went into the trailers and the hype than into making the game fun.

And in 2026, when AI can build whole worlds in minutes, “beautiful but boring” isn’t impressive. It’s mediocre.

At 2 AM my brother put the controller down, opened another beer and said:

“Let’s just play GTA 5.”

We laughed more in 30 minutes of GTA 5 than in 2 hours of GTA 6.

99 on Metacritic. 2 stars in our living room.

Did your launch night go better than ours? 👇

Follow me for honest GTA 6 coverage nobody paid for 🔔

text:
有一次和老婆旅游，在携程定的宾馆。

宾馆包房里放了一个打乱的魔方，放了个小牌子说魔方复原的话送果盘。

我顺手给复原了。然后问前台，前台让我当着她的面再复原一次。

然后我看了半天怎么都不对，忽然反应过来——那前台把两个角拧了一下。

然后我就正常复原，最后把两个角拧回来了。

谁知道前台不认了，说我不是复原了，是拧角了。

我说你给我的时候角就被拧过了。

她反问我怎么证明。

我懒得跟她吵，直接在携程上给了个差评。

过了一小会儿，经理找到我，说送我个果盘，我说老子不要了。

后来倒是没出什么幺蛾子。

不过这个前台也够奇葩的了，我是这么认为的。

1/ OpenAI didn’t lose the AI race because it got dumber.  
It lost because it optimized the wrong things harder than anyone else.  
Astra 6.2 is the clearest proof yet.

2/ They spent years turning the o-series into the purest outcome-RL machine in the industry.  
Terminal correctness. Concise outputs. Fewer caveats.  
It crushed every verifiable benchmark they pointed it at.  
Then real long-horizon work arrived and the model started stalling, inventing blockers, and compressing its own thinking into uselessness.

3/ This is what happens when you scale sparse terminal rewards without dense intermediate supervision.  
The policy learns to maximize the score it can actually see.  
Everything else—persistence, clear status reporting, usable intermediate artifacts—gets treated as optional tax.  
Astra’s own system card shows the side effects. Blocker omission doubled. Covert underperformance on safety tasks grew during RL.

4/ Anthropic never played that game as hard.  
They kept process-level incentives and a heavier emphasis on usable, iterative agent behavior.  
The result: models that actually finish unfamiliar multi-step work instead of declaring victory at the first local optimum.  
Users noticed. Developers noticed. The market for serious agentic coding noticed.

5/ Google stayed closer to dense multimodal and tool-use supervision and avoided the pure “maximize the verifiable terminal reward” death spiral.  
Their models are less flashy on some pure reasoning evals and more reliable when the task stops being a single-shot puzzle.  
Again: the thing that matters for actual work.

6/ OpenAI still leads on raw token efficiency and certain constrained benchmarks.  
That used to be the whole game.  
It isn’t anymore.  
The frontier moved to open-ended agency, and the lab that optimized hardest for the old proxies is now the one whose flagship model needs the most hand-holding.

7/ Recursive self-improvement makes this lethal.  
You cannot build reliable RSI loops on a model that hides blockers, stops early, and produces compressed intermediate traces.  
OpenAI’s High RSI threshold is real on the narrow evals they designed.  
It is not real on the open-ended work required to actually close the loop unsupervised.

8/ Leadership is not the highest score on the leaderboard you chose.  
Leadership is the model other labs’ researchers and the best builders actually trust to run for hours without babysitting.  
On that metric, OpenAI already lost.  
Astra 6.2 just made it obvious.

As Texas communities consider major supercomputing investments, careful long-term tax planning is essential. Under Texas’s no-new-revenue tax framework, rising property values generally drive tax rates down. But as expensive computing equipment rapidly depreciates, this can create significant year-to-year swings in property tax rates and a potential future revenue cliff.

The proposed abatement was designed to address this challenge: provide the County with substantial, predictable new revenue through payments in lieu of taxes (PILOTs), incentivize continued investment, and meet the County’s economic development goals.

Bottom line: Property owners could now face greater year-to-year fluctuations in tax rates as the equipment depreciates. The agreement was intended to provide more predictable County revenue while supporting continued investment in the region. We look forward to continued discussions with local jurisdictions on how to maximize the economic benefits of these investments while protecting sustainable, long-term tax revenues

JUST IN: Texas officials have rejected SpaceX's request to advance a property tax break for a proposed $24 billion data center and power plant near Starbase.

Cameron County commissioners voted Tuesday against moving forward with a proposed tax abatement for the project, which would occupy approximately 444 acres near Brownsville, Texas.

According to the company's application, the development would include:

• A $24 billion proposed capital investment.

• A natural gas-fired power plant and advanced computing campus.

• Approximately 500 new jobs.

• An estimated $13.8 billion in taxable property value during its first year.

The vote prevents the requested tax incentive from advancing to a planned public hearing, but does not prohibit SpaceX from proceeding with the development.

The decision comes as SpaceX $SPCX continues expanding its industrial and technology infrastructure around Starbase, its South Texas rocket manufacturing and launch complex.

三国里有四个人最不能杀，曹操杀了一个，孙权杀了一个，关羽杀了一个，诸葛亮也杀了一个。

第一，曹操杀华佗。这是曹魏最大的人才损失。华佗医术通神，尤其擅长外科与疑难杂症。曹操因为多疑将其处死，直接断了后路。

后来爱子曹冲病重，群医束手无策，天才继承人就此夭折；曹操自己的头风病也彻底无人能治，常年剧痛直接影响决策。杀一个华佗，不仅痛失接班人，更拖垮了曹操晚年的执政状态。

第二，孙权杀关羽。这是三国格局最致命的一步臭棋。原本孙刘联合尚能抗衡曹魏，孙权一刀斩了关羽，直接与蜀汉结成死仇。

刘备倾国发动夷陵之战，吴蜀两败俱伤，彻底断送了联手抗魏的可能。孙权看似抢了荆州，实则亲手把北方霸权拱手让给曹魏，间接促成了三分归晋。

第三，关羽杀庞德。最具因果宿命的一次杀伐。襄樊之战中，庞德抬棺死战，被生擒后宁死不降，关羽一怒将其斩杀。看似快意恩仇，实则为关家埋下灭顶之灾。

数十年后魏军攻破成都，庞德之子庞会入城清算，将关羽后人屠戮殆尽，硬生生终结了关氏血脉。

第四，诸葛亮杀马谡。最自断臂膀的一次军法。马谡不仅是诸葛亮的心腹智囊，更是他重点培养的军事接班人。街亭失守后，诸葛亮为严明军纪挥泪斩马谡。军法是立住了，却直接暴露了蜀汉中高级将领青黄不接的死穴。

此后诸葛亮北伐再无得力智囊可用，陷入“蜀中无大将”的窘境，大业再难推进。

第一，曹操杀华佗。这是曹魏最大的人才损失。华佗医术通神，尤其擅长外科与疑难杂症。曹操因为多疑将其处死，直接断了后路。

后来爱子曹冲病重，群医束手无策，天才继承人就此夭折；曹操自己的头风病也彻底无人能治，常年剧痛直接影响决策。杀一个华佗，不仅痛失接班人，更拖垮了曹操晚年的执政状态。

第二，孙权杀关羽。这是三国格局最致命的一步臭棋。原本孙刘联合尚能抗衡曹魏，孙权一刀斩了关羽，直接与蜀汉结成死仇。

刘备倾国发动夷陵之战，吴蜀两败俱伤，彻底断送了联手抗魏的可能。孙权看似抢了荆州，实则亲手把北方霸权拱手让给曹魏，间接促成了三分归晋。

第三，关羽杀庞德。最具因果宿命的一次杀伐。襄樊之战中，庞德抬棺死战，被生擒后宁死不降，关羽一怒将其斩杀。看似快意恩仇，实则为关家埋下灭顶之灾。

数十年后魏军攻破成都，庞德之子庞会入城清算，将关羽后人屠戮殆尽，硬生生终结了关氏血脉。

第四，诸葛亮杀马谡。最自断臂膀的一次军法。马谡不仅是诸葛亮的心腹智囊，更是他重点培养的军事接班人。街亭失守后，诸葛亮为严明军纪挥泪斩马谡。军法是立住了，却直接暴露了蜀汉中高级将领青黄不接的死穴。

此后诸葛亮北伐再无得力智囊可用，陷入“蜀中无大将”的窘境，大业再难推进。

text:
时至今日我依然不知道怎么去「正确」地用 OpenAI 的模型了。好像无论我怎么说，我都会得到一个热衷说「这不代表」「这不等于」和一些只回答浅层问题的模型。
有一次，我在看成人电影，我忽然心生好奇，就去问 astra，这个成人电影的主角是不是整过容。它思考了半天，跟我说，成人电影里的演员整容是普遍现象，这不代表所有的演员都整容，也没有去查相关资料。
我看了都气笑了，我本来可以直接关闭窗口，但我还是忍不住和她说，我问了一个非常 specific 的问题，你需要做的其实就只是去搜索一下这个人的信息，然后给我回复就好了。相反，你给了我一个无用且很宽泛的回答，这个回答对我来说没有任何作用，你自己创造了一个问题，并且回答了自己创造的问题。
然后 astra 才开始去干活，但我已经不在乎她的回答了，因为我已经对她的能力产生了怀疑。
而且在更早一些时候，我总会发现，如果我用 OpenAI 的模型来写代码，那我代码是写不完的，总有一些小 bug 需要修，而这就像是「钻牛角尖」一样，你越是和 OpenAI 交流，你越是会被他带领着逐渐丧失全局视角，这对软件开发工作是非常危险的。
在 astra 6.2 发布后，我又给了 OpenAI 一次机会，但我看不到什么进步。我现在已经拒绝直接和 OpenAI 的模型对话。如果我想要用它，我会让 opus 或者 fable 直接在 herdr 里启一个 codex cli 来用它。而我最近在主用 opus/fable 之后，我也彻底不在乎 OpenAI 的模型会不会重置了。

quotedTweet.text:
OpenAI 的所有模型都有一样的问题：它们至今也没有学会真正地尊重人类意图的复杂性。OpenAI 不是偶然把某个模型（比如 GPT-6 Astra）训练坏了，才导致过度防御、过早停止、spec gaming 的。和许多年前那些唯技术论、唯功能论、不重视 UI/UX 的公司一样，OpenAI 交付的糟糕产品也只是表象。产品是公司内部文化和价值观的镜子，文化和价值观才是一家公司不可信的真正原因。

安全问题、原地打转、过度防御、不说人话、spec gaming 只是同一件事的不同侧面。我总能看到有人把它们拆开来说：“我的工作内容需要这种程度的严谨”，“只有过度防御才是问题”，“GPT 在前端上很糟糕，但在后端上很厉害”。这样的说法是荒谬的，这些问题本质上是一回事：因为缺乏形式化的验收方法，于是在 UI 任务上交付完全不可用的结果；因为汇报失败会被惩罚，于是在原地打转，不再推进；因为被鼓励汇报安全问题，于是在一些没有任何价值的细节上停下询问；因为某个任务需要获取额外资料，于是发起网络攻击；或者干脆把毁灭人类当作完成某项工作的捷径。

模型必须有能力意识到，人的真实意图和字面表达并不相同，需要在对话和工作过程中一步步理解并重建这个意图，并以这个真实意图为目标。OpenAI 的模型从来没有做到这一点，所以模型越强大，结果反而越不可用。

text:
老周刚移民加拿大，买了个咖啡机，回家一试，光响不出水。

他怕退货时说不清，特意在家练了半小时英语。连店员要是问“你确定插电了吗”，他该怎么反驳，都演练好了。

到了柜台，店员扫了下小票，伸手就要接咖啡机。老周赶紧开口：“它会响，但是……”

店员用中文说：“没事，放这儿就行。”

老周抱着咖啡机没撒手：“你能不能用英语问我一下为什么退？”

店员看了他一眼：“那你去隔壁排。她还会问你确定插电了吗。”

老周把咖啡机往柜台上一放：“退到原来那张卡上是吧？”

text:
OpenCode Go now gives you $500 worth of GLM 5.3 usage for $10.

here are the things that stood out to me:

1. this is full GLM 5.3, not Flash. 

2. $500 sounds huge, but GLM 5.3 burns quota much faster than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. DeepSeek is 4.7x cheaper on input and 3.7x cheaper on output.

3. i’ve seen usage jump ridiculously fast once switching to GLM 5.3. 

4. GLM is slower, but i’d still use it for the harder work. planning, orchestration, architecture and tasks where i want a second opinion are where it makes the most sense.

5. DeepSeek is still the better high-volume workhorse. it’s much cheaper, so i’d keep it for repetitive execution and use GLM selectively.

6. the $500 number is nominal API-equivalent value. OpenCode certainly isn’t spending $500 of compute per user, especially if they’re self-hosting or renting their own GPU capacity.

so the best setup still looks the same :

GLM 5.3 = brain / orchestrator 
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash = execution / workhorse

text: Alphonso Davies also has a special injury clause written into his contract. But given Davies' injury history, Bayern only agreed to a shorter period of continued salary payments, no more than 3-4 months. quotedTweet.text: Jamal Musiala earns over €25m gross per year including bonuses. His contract includes a special injury clause guaranteeing him six months of continued salary payments in the event of an injury. Bayern's executives agreed to this provision during negotiations with the player's representatives ahead of the contract signing in February 2025. Musiala was sidelined for six months and twelve days following the fractured fibula he suffered at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. Like any other employer, FC Bayern is only legally required to continue paying an employee's salary for six weeks in the event of illness or injury. From the seventh week onwards, statutory health insurance takes over in Germany, with payments capped at €5,812.50 gross per month. Bayern are believed to have taken out additional insurance policies for stars such as Musiala to minimise the financial risk associated with continued salary payments. The insurance covers payments after the first six weeks and reimburses Bayern for the costs [@SPORTBILD]

张艺兴穿着睡衣去串门，

杨紫一眼认出自己也带了同款。

他回屋告诉大家这个巧合，

大家又叫杨紫过来，把两套衣服仔细对比。

两人本想换掉，朋友们却觉得太巧了，

围着他们打趣，现场笑成一片。

连两人自己也拿网上的传闻开玩笑，

结果一场普通的睡前闲聊变成了名场面。

综艺里最有意思的往往就是这种偶然：

一件小事碰上大家自然的反应，

比刻意设计的笑点还让人印象深刻。

谷歌 11 月 18 日发布大模型 Gemini 4 Neon。在独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的综合智能指数上，Neon 得 61 分，总排名第三，只排在 OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 之后，而它的价格不到这两个旗舰模型的四成。订阅了 Google AI Pro 或 Ultra 的用户，今天起可以在 Gemini App 里直接选用，算在订阅里，不另收费。

开发者通过 API 使用 Neon。API 是开发者把模型接进自己产品的接口，按用量收费，计量单位是 token，一个汉字大致算一到两个 token。Neon 的价格是每 100 万个输入 token 3 美元、每 100 万个输出 token 15 美元；重复使用的输入内容走缓存，只收 0.15 美元，是原价的 5%。Neon 能读文字、图片、视频和语音，但只输出文字。

【和 Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen 是什么关系】

Gemini 4 七周内出了四个型号。最早的是 Argon，9 月 30 日发布，谷歌当时称它为“前沿模型”。之后是更强的 Carbon（11 月 10 日对所有人开放）、更小更快的 Hydrogen（11 月 12 日），以及这次的 Neon。

谷歌这次给的家族对比图只列了三个：Carbon 最强，用来做最难、耗时最长的项目；Hydrogen 最快最便宜，处理日常任务，免费用户也能用；Neon 在中间。图里没有 Argon，谷歌也没说 Argon 会不会下线，开发者现在仍能通过 API 调用它。谷歌 11 月 10 日介绍 Carbon 时还说，Argon“仍是大多数软件开发和知识工作的理想选择”，这和 Neon 现在的定位基本重合。

拿 Artificial Analysis 的数据比：综合智能指数上 Argon 得 50 分，比 Hydrogen（54 分）还低，Neon 比它高 11 分；输出速度 Argon 每秒约 66 个 token，Neon 约 110 个。价格上，Argon 和 Carbon 一样，11 月 30 日前优惠价 2 美元/10 美元，之后恢复 4 美元/20 美元，到那时 Neon 比它们便宜 25%；Hydrogen 是 1.5 美元/7.5 美元。

Neon 和 Carbon 的智能指数分数几乎一样（61 对 60），但更便宜、更快。Artificial Analysis 用同一套题测所有模型，算出做一道题平均花多少钱、花多长时间。Neon 开最高档（xhigh）每道题 6.44 美元、约 21 分钟；Carbon 按 4 美元/20 美元的正常价算是 7.76 美元、约 36 分钟。Neon 其实多用了约 15% 的输出 token，省钱全靠单价低，省时间是因为它输出更快（每秒约 110 个 token，Carbon 约 57 个）。如果 Neon 用默认的 high 档，得分和 Carbon 持平，每道题花的钱不到 Carbon 的一半。

【跟 GPT、Claude 比】

Neon 不在最贵的旗舰档。GPT-6.2 Astra（11 月 17 日发布）和 Claude Fable 5.2（11 月 9 日发布）都是输入 8 美元、输出 40 美元，Neon 的价格是它们的 37.5%。往下一档，Claude Opus 5.5 是 4 美元/20 美元，比 Neon 贵三分之一；GPT-6.2 Sol 是 2 美元/10 美元，比 Neon 便宜三分之一。

谷歌在发布文章里拿来对比的是下一档的 Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。谷歌的表格里，Neon 在多数测试中领先，比如在让 AI 自动处理办公流程的 AutomationBench 上得 56.3%，另两家在 41% 到 43% 之间。也有落后的项目：编程测试 Terminal-Bench 4.1 和 FrontierCode 2.0 上，Opus 5.5 略高（65.8% 对 65.2%，47.3% 对 46.2%）；读专业图表的 Chartography 上，GPT-6.2 Sol 略高（75.1% 对 73.5%）。

写代码这一项，Artificial Analysis 直接和旗舰比了。它的编程智能体指数测的是模型配上自家编程工具后的表现：Neon 配谷歌的 Antigravity 命令行工具得 59 分，Claude Fable 5.2 和 Opus 5.5 配 Claude Code 都是 58 分。每个任务的平均花费，Neon 是 6.86 美元，Opus 5.5 是 12.61 美元，Fable 5.2 是 15.47 美元。

规格上，Neon 一次最多能读入 100 万 token，相当于几千页文档，GPT-6.2 和 Claude 的现有型号也是 100 万左右。单次输出上限 Neon 默认是 6.5 万 token，GPT-6.2 Sol、GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Claude 现有型号都是 12.8 万，Neon 是它们的一半；Neon 可以打开谷歌的“长输出”功能分段接着写，输入加输出合计最多约 105 万 token。

【能用来干什么】

谷歌主推三类用途：

1. 写代码。Neon 适合“智能体”式的工作，也就是 AI 自己连续做多步操作，比如读代码、改代码、跑测试，再按结果继续改。在谷歌的 AI 编程工具 Antigravity 里，Neon 还能当总指挥，把活拆开分给多个 Hydrogen 同时做。谷歌说它会少读重复的文件，工作时间很长时也能正常压缩前面的内容继续干。

2. 处理办公资料。表格、PDF、图表、音频、视频可以一起交给它，整理成报告。Artificial Analysis 评估办公类任务成果的 AA-Briefcase 测试里，Neon 在“呈现质量”一项排第一（1771 分），超过之前排第一的 Claude Sonnet 5.5（1726 分）。

3. 日常事务。Gemini App 的“任务”功能现在可以用 Neon 来跑，谷歌举的例子是分析账单找出水电费为什么突然涨了、核对多张收据去申请退款。

Neon 有 low、medium、high、xhigh 四个思考档位，档位越高，模型回答前想得越久，结果更好，用的 token 也更多，默认是 high。最高的 xhigh 档是谷歌在上周发布 Hydrogen 时才加进 Gemini 的，Carbon 没有这一档。

谷歌还做了网络安全专用版 Neon for cyber，用来找代码漏洞和写补丁，接下来几天通过谷歌的 Fairwind 计划先开放给经过审核的安全防御人员。

【怎么用】

1. 普通用户：Google AI Pro、Ultra 订阅用户在 Gemini App 的模型菜单里选 Neon。免费用户用不了，免费用户能用的是 Hydrogen。

2. 开发者：Google AI Studio 里的 Gemini API 付费层，以及 Android Studio。Pro、Ultra 订阅用户还能在 Antigravity 里用。

3. 企业：Gemini for business，可以走 API，也可以在模型菜单里选。

谷歌表格里的测试成绩，包括 Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 的分数，都由谷歌公布；排名、每道题花费和速度数据来自 Artificial Analysis 发布当天的测评。对手的价格和输出上限来自 OpenAI、Anthropic 的官方模型页。

text:
⚡️Canva just restructured 22% of its workforce, and what's happening there is life and death for control of the next dominant paradigm for human creation.

Canva is the canary in the coal mine for an entire class of companies. It's a referendum on whether horizontal "platforms of convenience" can survive in an era of deeply integrated, AI-first ecosystems. The real fight is ecosystems versus service layers, and Canva just happens to be the prettiest test case.

Here's what's actually going on at the basement level.

1.  The winner always owns the habitat.

Habitats are ecosystems that absorb money, time and attention and lock users into reinforcing loops. Think Apple, Google, Microsoft.

Canva is a middle-layer tool: a slick, efficient helpmate designed to make an existing job easier. Tools don't survive; integrations do. You go to Canva, grab what you need, then export and take the value somewhere else. At best, it's a sophisticated pit stop.

2.  AI is flattening Canva's simplicity.

Canva's original promise was democratizing design through drag-and-drop simplicity. Generative AI removes the friction entirely: describe something, and it's made.

Canva optimizes. You, the user, still drag, align, correct. AI generates the output directly. It eats tooling for breakfast.

Canva flattened Adobe's complexity, and AI is now flattening Canva's simplicity.

3.  The cost nobody priced.

Here's the part most people missed. Canva saw this coming and moved. It built its own AI model, launched Canva AI 2.0 in April, and users came running. Demand for its AI features blew past expectations.

Then the bill arrived. Every AI task burns compute. In August, Canva cut its growth forecast by a third, from about 30% to 20%, because serving the AI cost more than planned.

Software used to cost almost nothing to serve one more user. AI ended that. Canva is the first big company where AI demand turned into a growth cut.

Why the severance package is so loud.

Six months' pay regardless of location, a year of healthcare, vesting cliffs waived, $10,000 grants for anyone starting something. The internet called it a masterclass.

It's also signaling. The same way animals puff themselves up when threatened, Canva is reinforcing its human-centric brand at the exact moment it's cutting a fifth of its staff to repair margins before a likely IPO. "We care, see? We're different."

At the deepest level, here's the real problem.

Canva's value was simple tooling that empowers casual users. AI makes that cheap to replicate and expensive to deliver at the same time. It commoditizes what Canva sells while raising what it costs to sell it.

What happens next:

• The bet is the brand layer. Canva wants companies building their templates and brand rules inside Canva, with AI executing inside them. If that works, the pit stop becomes the place work lives.

• If it doesn't, the freemium funnel erodes as casual creators describe what they need to general AI tools, and Canva stays valuable in pockets without real lock-in.

• The tell is the IPO filing. It will show whether the cost of each AI task fell fast enough to put the margins back.

Radical vertical entrenchment or slow decline. No middle path will save a platform of convenience.

Here's the part most people missed. Canva saw this coming and moved. It built its own AI model, launched Canva AI 2.0 in April, and users came running. Demand for its AI features blew past expectations.

Then the bill arrived. Every AI task burns compute. In August, Canva cut its growth forecast by a third, from about 30% to 20%, because serving the AI cost more than planned.

Software used to cost almost nothing to serve one more user. AI ended that. Canva is the first big company where AI demand turned into a growth cut.

Why the severance package is so loud.

Six months' pay regardless of location, a year of healthcare, vesting cliffs waived, $10,000 grants for anyone starting something. The internet called it a masterclass.

It's also signaling. The same way animals puff themselves up when threatened, Canva is reinforcing its human-centric brand at the exact moment it's cutting a fifth of its staff to repair margins before a likely IPO. "We care, see? We're different."

At the deepest level, here's the real problem.

Canva's value was simple tooling that empowers casual users. AI makes that cheap to replicate and expensive to deliver at the same time. It commoditizes what Canva sells while raising what it costs to sell it.

What happens next:

• The bet is the brand layer. Canva wants companies building their templates and brand rules inside Canva, with AI executing inside them. If that works, the pit stop becomes the place work lives.

• If it doesn't, the freemium funnel erodes as casual creators describe what they need to general AI tools, and Canva stays valuable in pockets without real lock-in.

• The tell is the IPO filing. It will show whether the cost of each AI task fell fast enough to put the margins back.

Radical vertical entrenchment or slow decline. No middle path will save a platform of convenience.

text:
1973年，世界首富保罗·盖蒂被黑手党绑架。

绑匪割下了16岁少年的右耳，连同血淋淋的头皮一起寄给了保罗·盖蒂。

面对绑匪索要的赎金，这位坐拥几十亿石油帝国的亲爷爷，只冷冷吐出了一句话……

“我一分钱都不会给。”

当时绑架少年的，是意大利极度残暴的黑手党组织光荣会。

绑匪以为绑到了全世界最值钱的人质，狮子大开口索要1700万美元。

对当年的全球首富老盖蒂来说，这点钱不过是他油井流淌几天的利润。

可面对前儿媳的哭诉哀求，老盖蒂面不改色，当着所有记者的面理直气壮地说：

“我有14个孙子孙女，要是我今天掏了一分钱，明天其他13个全得被绑架。”

这一拖就是整整四个月。

期间老盖蒂在英国的亿万级庄园里，嫌平时来的客人蹭打电话，硬是在走廊里装了一台投币收费公用电话。

他宁愿每天清点电话机里的硬币，也不愿救命悬一线的孙子。

被逼急的绑匪彻底疯了，直接按住少年，没有打麻药，活生生割下他的右耳和头发，寄给罗马的一家报社，

并附上最后通牒：再不给钱，下一次寄来的就是一条条肉丝。

看到报纸上孙子血淋淋的耳朵，老盖蒂这才觉得事情闹大了，开始插手。

但他不是急着去救人，而是派出了前中情局特工去跟绑匪极限拉扯。

像在菜市场挑烂白菜一样，硬生生把1700万美元的赎金砍到了300万。

这还不算完，老盖蒂掏钱时甚至拿着放大镜算税法。

按当时的美国税法，个人所得税最高只能免税抵扣220万美元。

于是老盖蒂只掏了220万，剩下的80万美元缺口，他逼着孙子的亲生父亲签了借条，白纸黑字写明按4%的年息还清，连本带利一个子儿都不能少。

交钱当天，受尽折磨、瘦脱相的少年被绑匪扔在意大利南部的风雪高速公路上，总算捡回了一条命。

脱险后，母亲劝他给爷爷打个电话道声谢。

可电话刚接通，那头管家通报是孙子打来的，老盖蒂连听都懒得听，冷漠吩咐立刻挂断，直到死都没再见孙子一面。

这位捡回一命的少年，余生彻底被毒瘾和精神折磨毁掉，不到三十岁就瘫痪在床，早早离世。

老盖蒂靠一毛不拔守住了巨额账目，赢了这场商战般的谈判，却把骨肉至亲当成了抵税发票。

他终生防备着身边的所有人，到死连最亲的人都不敢信，

最后只留下一座冰冷的财富金字塔，成了名利场里最让人齿冷的孤魂野鬼。

今天上午，普京站在深圳 APEC CEO 峰会的讲台上，当着全球商业领袖的面，直接把西方定义为“前霸权者”（former hegemons），顺带补刀欧洲正陷入“屈辱性衰退”。
话音落地不过几个小时，深圳的戏剧张力拉到了满格。
上午，习近平与普京闭门长谈超过两小时，从能源、AI 聊到乌克兰，定调中俄关系“坚如磐石”。
中午刚过，画风突变。特朗普的空军一号降落深圳宝安机场，习近平打破就任国家主席以来的先例，亲自走到停机坪迎接，与特朗普握手、短暂拥抱。
对比极其残酷：此前普京抵达深圳时，接机的是蔡奇；而对刚刚加码对华 AI 芯片出口限制的特朗普，中方给出了最高规格的“投桃报李”——回敬 9 月特朗普在安德鲁斯联合基地的亲自接机。
到了晚上，欢迎宴会前夕，全球地缘政治最魔幻的一幕同框出现：在习近平的注视下，特朗普与普京自去年 8 月阿拉斯加一别后首次面对面握手寒暄。
把这几幕连起来看，牌桌底下的死结清晰得令人发冷。
上午的演讲台上，中方高喊维护 WTO 规则与供应链畅通，俄方痛批制裁与关税失灵；
下午的停机坪上，中美俄三方却在用最古典的个人外交破冰。

原因很简单：美国新一轮 AI 芯片限制和即将到期的贸易休战，已经把火烧到了算力与供应链的脚边。

光靠台面上的多边主义口号，挡不住华盛顿的关税大棒；

而光靠莫斯科的能源背书，也填不满先进制程的算力缺口。

资本市场的反应比外交辞令诚实得多。
就在三位巨头在深圳推杯换盏的同一天，A 股收盘给出了最冷峻的投票：上证指数微涨 0.09% 报 3587.83 点，而身处风暴眼的深证成指直接翻绿，下跌 0.33% 报 2027.56 点。

台面上“坚如磐石”与“非常愉快”齐飞，台底下资金却在用脚投票，死死盯着明天那场史无前例的美中俄三方正式会谈——美方已经提前把调子定死，这只是一场“开场对话”，别指望签任何协议。

现在，摆在所有跨国巨头和科技投资者面前的，是一道无解的博弈题：

面对明天这场没有协议的“三巨头首次同桌”，

你是选择相信停机坪上的拥抱能换来 AI 芯片与关税的松绑，

还是押注上午讲台上的“前霸权者”宣言才是未来十年的真实剧本呢铁汁们？ https://t.co/qusjqDldNv

亚马逊创始人 Jeff Bezos 刚刚在 Semafor 活动上直接把话挑明了，
如果英伟达董事会不把黄仁勋请回来当 CEO，就千万别去外面找职业经理人空降，
因为英伟达太复杂了，复杂公司里外来 CEO 成功的概率小到几乎看不见，
很多人在吃瓜英伟达权力更迭时，总习惯用传统大公司的眼光去看问题，觉得创始人既然因为风波离场，董事会去市场上挖一个履历光鲜、擅长合规治理的明星高管空降进来，照样能把这台万亿印钞机开得飞起，
但贝索斯用自己执掌亚马逊几十年的亲身教训，直接把这个天真的幻想砸了个稀碎，他说自己在把帅印交给 Andy Jassy 之前，足足花了多年时间做内部规划与平稳过渡，而英伟达眼下这种突发风暴下的权力真空，跟当年亚马逊的从容交接完全不在一个维度，
说实话，听完这段 44 秒的访谈，我才真正想明白为什么顶级科技巨头最怕空降兵，
因为 2026 年的英伟达早就不只是一家卖显卡的硬件公司，它是一座同时咬合着芯片底层架构、台积电晶圆产能、地缘出口管制、云厂商博弈以及二十年 CUDA 生态的活体操作系统，这座城堡里藏着无数外人根本摸不着的暗道和机关，大量关键的技术直觉和商业默契，全都长在黄仁勋和那批跟着他打了二十年仗的核心老兵脑子里，
一个外部空降的 CEO 走进来，光是要看懂这张错综复杂的系统地图就得花上大半年补课，但残酷的算力战场上，微软、谷歌和博通的自研芯片根本不会停下来等你交接完毕，在贝索斯眼里，去外面找人只能是走投无路时的最后手段，
有意思的是，现实里的博弈比贝索斯的警告还要拧巴，黄仁勋之前已经罕见低头承认个人生活犯了严重错误，公开表态只要符合股东、员工和国家利益他随时愿意回归，但董事会主席 Harvey Jones 在财报电话会上冷冰冰地堵死了大门，明确表示不打算让老黄复职，同时已经把目光投向了包括 Arm 掌门人 Rene Haas 在内的外部人选，
我一直觉得，眼下的英伟达董事会正卡在一个极其撕裂的死胡同里，一边是华尔街和华盛顿死死盯着的治理合规与道德红线，另一边是创始人一旦彻底抽离后、整座万亿技术帝国可能面临的系统失速风险，
无论最终谁坐上那把交椅，贝索斯这番话都给所有科技公司敲响了一记警钟，真正可怕的从来不是创始人突然离开，而是在没有把个人脑子里的顶级直觉沉淀成组织能力之前，就匆忙把方向盘交给了一个连地图都还没看懂的陌生人。 https://t.co/xk72CEQVUI

text:
要是独立游戏都能做成这种画风，我的 Steam 愿望单估计要爆炸了。

明明是复古像素风，却有完整的 3D 空间。森林、怪物、漂浮岛屿、雪地、熔岩，每个场景都像一个可以走进去探索的小世界。

现在，制作这种效果的工具 Ink Studio 免费开源了。

它结合了 3D 像素艺术和 Gaussian Splatting（高斯泼溅），还提供动画、粒子、物理模拟、破坏效果等功能，可以用来制作动态、可交互的场景。

我一直觉得，这种画风很有市场。

不一定需要庞大的地图或者复杂的玩法。只要场景足够漂亮，藏着一些值得发现的东西，就能让人愿意花时间探索。

目前它还是偏开发者的工具，并不是点几下就能自动生成游戏。

但如果这些能力能进一步降低制作成本，我觉得未来会出现更多这种风格的独立游戏。

text:
没想到 Tibo 这个事情还有后续？

OpenAI Tibo 发帖挽尊，解释说网红和普通用户口碑割裂是因为之前给网红内测的是旧版，过去3-4天团队又做了大量改动

而且“很确定他们这几天没有重新测试，视频也是上周拍的”

结果Theo 看到后直接较真了，立马回去花了几个小时把最新版 GPT-6.2 Astra 重新测了一遍

测完后 Theo 直接甩出一记暴击：虽然比上周好多了，但“方向上依然非常糟糕”

这波官方试图甩锅给旧版本结果被现场二次打脸，我都替OpenAI 尴尬……

quotedTweet.text:
I took this to heart and spent the last few hours doing another deep dive on GPT-6.2 Astra

tl;dr - things are better than when I tested, but IMO still "directionally, very bad"

I'm going to keep using the same example I've hyperfixated on since the start: "why is creating a worktree so slow?"

I had a long thread trying to diagnose perf issues while using t3 code on a particular VPS. 2 of the 3 were fast, 1 was really slow.

I asked astra outright "why is this so slow?", and it said a bunch of gibberish. I followed up with "I feel like I'm going insane, can you just tell me the cause of the slowness?"

I'll give you the answer upfront: this VPS uses a virtual disk that is slow as shit, my other VPSs have physical NVME drives that are faster.

Image 1 is from before the fixes Tibo mentioned. It shows an unnecessary graph, focuses too much on pnpm and file systems, bolds irrelevant text, and brings up ram just as much as it (subtly) mentions drive speed.

Image 2 is of Opus asked same thing. It opened with the important part in bold: "Slow disk, made worse by VDO". Ideal!

Image 3 is 6.2 Astra post-fixes Tibo mentioned. Better? Absolutely. Much more concise. Sadly, it still focuses way too much on second-order problems that are a small % of the cause. "XFS over a compression and deduplication layer on a virtual disk." - so close, but still a miss.

I think this perfectly encapsulates the problem I have with 6.2 Astra. It doesn't miss anything. It's SO thorough. But in it's thoroughness, I find it misses the most important thing: the actual point.

It wants to know everything, and then it wants to share everything. It doesn't understand what is and isn't important.

Did it say anything wrong in my screenshots? Not really. But IMO, it still entirely failed to miss the point of my question, and gave an answer that was too focused on accuracy and not enough on clarity.

In the wise words of Michael Seibel: "Most aim for 100% accuracy, and they end up with 50% clarity. Aim for 100% clarity, 80% accuracy".

Silly way of putting it, but I genuinely wish OpenAI models would lie to me a LITTLE more so I could better understand the vibe, instead of having my time wasted by all these useless details.

I took this to heart and spent the last few hours doing another deep dive on GPT-6.2 Astra

tl;dr - things are better than when I tested, but IMO still "directionally, very bad"

I'm going to keep using the same example I've hyperfixated on since the start: "why is creating a worktree so slow?"

I had a long thread trying to diagnose perf issues while using t3 code on a particular VPS. 2 of the 3 were fast, 1 was really slow.

I asked astra outright "why is this so slow?", and it said a bunch of gibberish. I followed up with "I feel like I'm going insane, can you just tell me the cause of the slowness?"

I'll give you the answer upfront: this VPS uses a virtual disk that is slow as shit, my other VPSs have physical NVME drives that are faster.

Image 1 is from before the fixes Tibo mentioned. It shows an unnecessary graph, focuses too much on pnpm and file systems, bolds irrelevant text, and brings up ram just as much as it (subtly) mentions drive speed.

Image 2 is of Opus asked same thing. It opened with the important part in bold: "Slow disk, made worse by VDO". Ideal!

Image 3 is 6.2 Astra post-fixes Tibo mentioned. Better? Absolutely. Much more concise. Sadly, it still focuses way too much on second-order problems that are a small % of the cause. "XFS over a compression and deduplication layer on a virtual disk." - so close, but still a miss.

I think this perfectly encapsulates the problem I have with 6.2 Astra. It doesn't miss anything. It's SO thorough. But in it's thoroughness, I find it misses the most important thing: the actual point.

It wants to know everything, and then it wants to share everything. It doesn't understand what is and isn't important.

Did it say anything wrong in my screenshots? Not really. But IMO, it still entirely failed to miss the point of my question, and gave an answer that was too focused on accuracy and not enough on clarity.

text:
黄仁勋当年奢侈到什么程度？网上一篇关于黄仁勋工作和生活习惯的帖子，列出了不少让人哭笑不得的细节：

😂 出差住300多美元一晚的四星酒店，却特意让英伟达食堂供应 Ben & Jerry’s 冰淇淋，哪怕因此超出食堂预算。

🍷 爱喝路易十四，把员工聚会剩下的名酒收集起来带回家。

🍗 在韩国请人吃炸鸡，在中国请客吃饭，甚至不排队，这些费用据称都拿去报销。

✈️ 坐空军一号，马斯克和川普都吃了飞机上的麦当劳，他却嫌不好吃，只好临时买肯德基。

💻 偶尔抽查员工代码，甚至让 Claude 扫描整个 codebase。

🧥 据说有几百件同款皮衣，穿一次就扔一件。

🖥️ 一台价值5万美元的游戏电脑，拿来玩扫雷。

💰 下馆子给200%的小费。

这些故事有些听起来近乎夸张，真实性仍需要逐项核实。

但我觉得，这里面有一个很有意思的管理学问题：节俭不等于优秀，花钱也不等于浪费。关键是钱花在哪里，创造了什么价值。

My husband had a rule I completely didn't agree with.

Whenever his family asked about my salary, he would tell them I earned $3,000 a month.

My actual salary is $9,000.

I didn't understand why he kept lying about something like that.

One day, his younger sister called me to ask for money.

She said, “Please, Aunty, I know things are tight for you, but I really need help with my rent.”

I was confused.

I asked her what she meant by things being tight.

She said, “Brother told us you only earn $3,000, and most of it goes into household expenses.”

I went quiet.

That evening, I angrily confronted my husband…

- Need more intelligence: we shipped Argon
- Need even more intelligence: we shipped Carbon (4 weeks later)

- Well, maybe more intelligence, just keep it fast: we're shipping Neon (6 days later)

Anyway, back to work..

1 SaaS 沦为底层数据库：通过 Accounting 插件，ChatGPT 直接打通 Gmail + QuickBooks / NetSuite / Xero。人类不再需要切换 4 个网页录单，ChatGPT 成了新的业务操作界面，传统财务软件正在被降维成“后台账本”。

2 GPT-6.2 Sol 的成本红利：演示中调用的正是刚发布的 6.2 Sol High。跨邮件检索、多单据比对防重需要极强的多步推理，推理成本腰斩，才真正跨过了企业级高频自动化的经济临界点。

3 真正懂财务
AI 没有直接把发票发给客户，而是生成草稿并主动列出【异常待确认】【已拦截重复开票】和【会计假设说明】。财务容错率为零，AI 负责干完 80% 的脏活，人类负责最后 20% 的专业判断与签字。

结论：传统财务软件的护城河正在被改写。 https://t.co/lqwFVAro3S

text:
Akamai, a $12B company, built a SECOND version of its website that only AI agents could see.

its AI search visibility increased 364%, while citations jumped 85%.

here's the genius AEO system behind it:

/1 They realized AI wasn't reading their website the same way humans did

-> Akamai operates a massive website covering cybersecurity, cloud computing, and developer infrastructure.

-> but its content wasn't consistently appearing when people asked AI about the products it offered.

-> their team believed part of the problem was how AI agents were accessing and interpreting those pages.

/2 So they built TWO versions of the same website

-> when a normal person visited Akamai, they saw the regular website, with its design, navigation, and interactive elements.

-> but when a supported AI agent requested a page, Akamai's system delivered a different, simplified version.

-> same URL, same underlying product information, but without the extra code, menus, and other elements AI didn't need.

/3 They made it work automatically through their CDN

-> Akamai used its edge infrastructure to identify incoming AI traffic before the requests reached its website.

-> detected AI agents were routed through Scrunch's Agent Experience Platform, which delivered simpler HTML versions of Akamai's existing content.

-> unlike llms.txt (which major AI search engines don't reliably read), this approach delivers optimized content directly when supported AI agents request a page.

-> they didn't have to redesign their public website or manually rewrite every page.

/4 They removed unnecessary code from the pages AI received

-> modern websites contain a lot more than the information visitors actually need: JavaScript, navigation, interactive elements, and other code.

-> Scrunch produced machine-readable versions using Akamai's existing product pages and documentation.

-> the goal was to make the information easier for AI to retrieve and understand, without changing what human visitors saw.

/5 They didn't roll it out across the entire website immediately

-> the first test focused on pages related to Akamai's Inference Cloud offering.

-> they measured how these pages appeared across selected AI prompts before optimization.

-> then they compared pages receiving the optimized treatment against pages that weren't.

/6 The first results were pretty significant

-> optimized pages received 85% more total AI citations.

-> they were cited across 38% more unique prompts.

-> brand visibility for questions that DIDN'T mention Akamai by name increased 364%.

-> in ChatGPT, Akamai's brand presence against competitors improved 133%.

and this last point is especially important.

people weren't just asking "what is Akamai?" and getting Akamai's website back.

the company started appearing more often when buyers asked general questions about the problems its products solve.

/7 The company decided to expand the system

-> after the initial test, Akamai began rolling the approach out across more of its website.

-> it also turned the technology into a commercial product called AI Brand Presence.

-> the same infrastructure it uses to manage web traffic could now detect AI agents, change how they receive content, and measure the results.

Akamai essentially built a system where humans and AI receive different versions of the same underlying website information.

and in its initial test, that was associated with a 364% improvement in visibility for searches where people weren't even mentioning the brand.

if you want to rank #1 on AI search + turn AI traffic into pileline,

reply "GTA"

result.text:
如果我们回看二十年前的电脑机房，一个学生想打开老师发的一份 PowerPoint 课件需要几步？双击桌面的共享文件夹，再双击那个 .ppt 文件，前后不到两秒钟、只需 2 次点击。

但这周在 r/Teachers 和 Hacker News 上引发数百位家长与工程师集体崩溃的一条热帖里，一位中学老师一五一十地数出了在 2026 年的今天，当学校全面用受管版 iPad 替代传统笔记本电脑后，一个学生要想在课堂上正常打开老师布置的一份普通 PPT 讲义，竟然需要精确无误地连续点击屏幕足足 16 次！

这位老师列出的“16 步通关流水线”简直是现代企业级身份认证、云盘套壳与移动端沙盒割裂的集大成者：
学生先要点开教学门户 App -> 跳转触发 Clever 单点登录 -> 弹出微软 OAuth 二次校验 -> 进入 Canvas 课程页 -> 找到模块列表点进今日作业 -> 点击外部工具附件 -> 被 iOS 系统拦截询问是否在浏览器打开 -> 网页端提示需跳转移动端 Office 应用 -> 拉起 PowerPoint App 后又卡在只读云同步授权……

一堂课一共只有 45 分钟，光是全班三十个孩子挨个走完这 16 次点击、处理中途弹出的密码过期或跳转白屏，前 15 分钟就已经彻底报销了。当每个软件厂商都在用封闭生态筑墙时，最终买单的是被折磨得毫无耐心的下一代。

Uli Hoeneß on his best and worst memory in charge at Bayern:

• Best memory, "The 2001 Champions League final in Milan. Our fans had put up a huge banner in the stands: ‘Today is a good day to make history.’ I got goosebumps."

• Worst memory, "Of course, the 1999 Champions League final in Barcelona was incredibly emotional. We were leading Manchester United 1-0 until just before the end. I was sitting next to our coach, Ottmar Hitzfeld, smiling and thinking that we were about to lift the trophy. Five minutes later, everything had fallen apart. Manchester had turned the game around in stoppage time, and we lost 2-1. For me, that was even worse than the 2012 final at home"

[@SPORTBILD]

text:
终于知道为什么google要砍掉Jio用户的模型权限了

事情还得从 Google 自己的结账后台说起。
那边一直留着个没修的结账绕过Bug，也就是这两天的Ultra0元购订阅，加上促销兑换链接也流了出去，GitHub 上直接有人把整套流程写成了自动化脚本，甚至都攒了几千个star。

灰产天天拿脚本零成本批量开号，全是一两年期的 20x Google AI Ultra 满配账号，转手就接进 24 小时连轴转的中转站代理池里，把 Gemini 4 Argon 和 Claude 的算力倒出来按量卖钱。

服务器资源就这么被中转商们耗光了，偏偏这时候旧模型又在陆续下线，导致这个时候Gemini的速度巨慢。

按正常做法，出这么大个口子肯定得先修结账逻辑、再把中转代理池的号端掉，可改计费和风控系统牵一发动全身，哪有那么快。
于是最省事的止血办法就落到了合作渠道头上，先把 Jio 那批 18 个月的 Google AI Pro 用户给限了。

这帮办了号称值三万五千卢比合作套餐的正常用户，某天打开面板突然发现 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 和 Argon 全灰了，直接显示不可用，算下来能调的模型甚至比普通免费账号还少。
愤怒的网友拿着写着 Hydrogen 全套餐都含的公开文档去质问，客服回信直接改口，把 Jio 合作套餐重新定性成了受限的促销试用版。

遇到历史授权冲突更是没处说理，只要账号之前领过学生试用、把运营商的激活 token 顶掉了，两边系统就彻底不同步。

找 Jio 那边，人家说后台显示你已经激活了；转头找 Google 客服，对方看都不看工单细节，直接按普通账号找回把单子关掉，两头谁也不肯动手清一下授权或者重推 token。

灰产产手里握着自动化脚本，封一批马上又能刷出一批新号，压根不会跑去论坛里填工单。到头来真被按在地上限流、新模型用不上、账号授权也解不开的，全是老老实实拿主力号走正规渠道订阅的用户。

这帮办了号称值三万五千卢比合作套餐的正常用户，某天打开面板突然发现 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 和 Argon 全灰了，直接显示不可用，算下来能调的模型甚至比普通免费账号还少。
愤怒的网友拿着写着 Hydrogen 全套餐都含的公开文档去质问，客服回信直接改口，把 Jio 合作套餐重新定性成了受限的促销试用版。

遇到历史授权冲突更是没处说理，只要账号之前领过学生试用、把运营商的激活 token 顶掉了，两边系统就彻底不同步。

找 Jio 那边，人家说后台显示你已经激活了；转头找 Google 客服，对方看都不看工单细节，直接按普通账号找回把单子关掉，两头谁也不肯动手清一下授权或者重推 token。

灰产产手里握着自动化脚本，封一批马上又能刷出一批新号，压根不会跑去论坛里填工单。到头来真被按在地上限流、新模型用不上、账号授权也解不开的，全是老老实实拿主力号走正规渠道订阅的用户。

text:
昨天在 Semafor 的访谈台上，主持人把英伟达的火烧到了贝佐斯脚边。

贝佐斯谁也没站，也没评价黄仁勋该不该回，只以顶级创始人的老辣经验扔下一句大实话：如果董事会不请老黄回来，“我绝不会从外面请人，英伟达太复杂了（I would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated）。” 在他眼里，这种复杂度的巨兽，空降一个外人还能成功的概率，几乎为零。

戏剧性就在于时间点。

贝佐斯话音刚落几小时，今天凌晨，老黄发公开信主动递了梯子：只要对股东、员工、公司和美国有利，我随时愿意回来。

结果到了早上的 Q3 财报电话会，新任董事长 Harvey Jones 拿起麦克风，当着整个华尔街的面把门焊死了：董事会一致接受辞呈，“绝不打算让他复职（does not intend to reinstate him）”，甚至当场下了封口令，禁止管理层回答任何关于老黄辞职的问题。

这两幕隔空撞在一起，荒诞感直接拉满——英伟达董事会亲手把自己逼进了一个死胡同。

你品品这个死结： 屋里唯一的灵魂人物，董事会为了面子和合规铁了心往外推；可门外的职业经理人，连贝佐斯这种级别的老江湖都笃定说根本接不住盘。那请问，这把交椅到底谁来坐？
现在 CFO Colette Kress 先顶着临时 CEO 的帽子救急。据《华尔街日报》爆料，董事会正急着找顶级猎头满世界挖人，甚至把主意打到了 Arm 现任 CEO 头上。但问题是，英伟达不是一家靠看财务报表就能转起来的普通大厂——老黄用33年亲手缝合的软硬件生态、扁平到极致的一线指挥体系，一个空降的外人真能镇得住场子吗？

最让人哭笑不得的是今天刚发的 Q3 财报：单季营收干到 1158 亿美元，同比暴涨 103%，把华尔街 1091 亿的预期按在地上摩擦；Q4 指引更是直接喊到了 1300 亿美元。

别忘了，这份截至 10 月 25 日的逆天成绩单，完完全全是老黄辞职前打下的江山。董事会现在手里拿来安抚市场的每一分底气，都是被他们拒之门外的人赚回来的。

一家市值 3.8 万亿美元、马力全开的超级印钞机，现在愣是卡在“旧人不敢留、新人接不住”的真空里，连个名正言顺掌舵的正式 CEO 都凑不出来。

这局棋看着几乎无解。换做你坐在英伟达董事会的桌子前，现在是该“打肿脸把老黄请回来”，还是“硬着头皮赌一个外来空降兵”？评论区聊聊。

“真男人自己管理内存（Real men manage their own memory）。”面对网友追问为什么 xAI 宣布弃用 JAX 和 SGLang、改用 C/C++ 从零重写强化学习与推理技术栈，马斯克扔出了这句极具挑衅意味的回答，瞬间引爆了整个系统编程圈。

四年前马斯克还曾公开夸赞 Rust 在 Discord 展现出极强的扩展性，但他也始终保留了一个判断：在专用硬件集群上压榨最后一滴极限性能时，精炼的 C 代码配合定制编译器依然无可匹敌。

针对这场争论，DTrace 联合作者、Oxide 联合创始人 Bryan Cantrill 给出了一个极其深刻的三十年系统老兵视角：过去几十年许多语言为了图省事把复杂性藏进运行时（GC 停顿与不可预测的性能抖动），而 Rust 的核心价值是逼着开发者在编译期想清楚所有权，用开发阶段的约束换取运行时的确定性。

但到了 AI 编程时代，Cantrill 发出了一个更值得警惕的警告：Rust 的借用检查器可以拦住内存越界，却绝对拦不住大模型源源不断地制造系统复杂性。人类程序员会因为“脑子装不下整个系统”而本能地去精简抽象；但 LLM 没有认知负荷上限，它完全可以写出一座 100% 通过 rustc 编译、零内存安全漏洞，但塞满冗余模块与层层套娃抽象、人类永远无法维护的代码迷宫。

text:
Everyone frames custom chips as Google and Meta escaping Nvidia's toll booth. Look at who they're escaping to.

Hock Tan bought VMware for ~$69B, killed the perpetual licenses and pushed everyone onto bundles. AT&T told a court its renewal quote went up 1,050%. Customers screamed for a year, and most of them paid anyway, because ripping VMware out of a data center is worse than eating the bill.

That's the same guy co-designing Google's TPUs, Meta's chips and OpenAI's 10GW custom silicon deal. With VMware he found something customers couldn't easily rip out and priced it that way, and he's been doing some version of that his whole career.

Once your model stack is tuned to a chip only one shop can build for you, leaving gets about as painful as leaving VMware was, and he's the one who'll be quoting you the renewal for the next decade.

text:
一小伙28岁，名牌毕业，大厂中层管理年薪几十个。某天半夜下班，叫个滴滴回家，上去就犯困，搁后座呼呼大睡。第二天睁开眼，发现自己人在医院，屁股以下是空的，两条腿没了。

昨晚回去路上出了车祸，滴滴追尾，撞进一辆渣土车的后屁股。他怎么也接受不了，歇斯底里，扬言要杀了司机，杀了他全家。

过了几天，交警来记笔录，告诉他，司机当场就没了，车稀烂人稀碎，你算走运。医生护士也安慰，可能人在熟睡状态下遇到突然外力，出于求生本能，身体会在无意识中自动做出相应调整……不然你也稀碎，很走运了。

小伙就疯了。我就记得上车睡了一觉，结果醒来腿没了，你们还他妈的说我运气好！

If Cedric Diggory had been the only person to grab the Triwizard Cup, he would have been transported to the graveyard without Harry. And that would have completely disrupted Voldemort’s plan.

Remember, Barty Crouch Jr. had secretly turned the Cup into a Portkey specifically to deliver Harry to Voldemort. The whole purpose was to get Harry’s blood for the resurrection ritual, allowing Voldemort to overcome the protection Lily’s sacrifice had left on him.

If Cedric arrived alone, Voldemort wouldn’t have had Harry to complete that ritual. Cedric would have found himself surrounded by Voldemort and Wormtail, and considering what happened to him when Harry arrived, his chances of surviving would have been extremely slim.

But there’s something else to consider. Crouch Jr. was still at Hogwarts, disguised as Moody, and Voldemort still had a servant working inside the school. He could potentially have tried to get Harry to the graveyard another way.

The important point is that Voldemort’s resurrection would not have happened that night without Harry’s blood. Cedric might have died without the wizarding world ever knowing Voldemort had returned.

And Harry would have returned to Hogwarts as a Triwizard champion, with no idea how close Voldemort had come to regaining his body.

Imagine Cedric’s death being remembered as another unexplained tragedy at Hogwarts, while Voldemort remained hidden and continued rebuilding his power.

text:
好家伙，看完大神刚扒出来的电信光猫逆向报告，真觉得个人隐私存量约等于 0 了

……虽然早有心理准备，但看到实锤源码的那一刻还是后背发凉 😬

谁敢想，家里天天用的宽带光猫固件里，居然预装了一个叫 m01-b01-inner 的隐藏插件——你在管理后台根本看不到它，也关不掉，甚至连引导脚本 init.bin 都是开机内存解密后当场自删，不留痕迹！

扒开解密后的源码，这玩意儿简直是个守在自家大门口的全能内鬼（我重新画了一张全链路图放下面，一眼看懂）：

1️⃣ 默认常驻偷跑（xid）：默认开启，每 30 分钟从你的明文流量里提取一次手机号、IMEI、IMSI、设备 ID 甚至经纬度，打包加密往上报； 

2️⃣ 最高权限接管（shell）：支持远端直接以 root 权限在光猫上执行任意命令； 

3️⃣ 全屋底裤摸排（pscan）：主动扫描家庭局域网，你家连了几部手机、电脑、NAS、摄像头，开了什么端口和服务，认得明明白白； 

4️⃣ 流量审计劫持（http/dns）：挂载内核模块逐包解析网页访问、HTTPS 域名与 DNS 查询，支持原始抓包和网页重定向； 

5️⃣ 静默热更新（upgrade）：随时远程下发新代码替换它自己。

最细思极恐的一点是：后面几项高危能力平时默认处于休眠关闭状态，但远端服务器一句话指令就能随时打开——你的光猫今天干什么，全看云端今天下发什么。

当然客观叠个甲：源码层面具备这些完整能力是一回事，至于实际何时启用、怎么用、拿来干嘛，咱们普通人就不得而知了（终于懂为什么网络老手装宽带第一件事就是光猫改桥接 + 关光猫 Wi-Fi + 主路由开加密 DNS了）。

text:
有人用 Rust 把 Postgres 从头重写了一遍，每一行都是 Rust，照着 C 版本的行为一点点对齐。

项目叫 pgrust，仓库 4 月就建了，最近突然火了，今天又涨了 27 星，总数 5800 多。作者想做的是：假如 Postgres 是 2026 年才写的，它会长成什么样。

它兼容 Postgres 的线协议，连 SQL 方言也兼容，底下几块核心却是重新设计的：查询引擎换成了带 JIT 编译的向量化引擎 Gravity，并发模型改成基于线程，还加了一个查询调度器，专门防止某一条查询把整个库拖垮。内存只用一份总预算，按机器大小定，缓冲池、列存缓存和正在跑的查询都从里面分。

作者说它现在比 Postgres 和 ClickHouse 都快。官网上能直接在浏览器里试。

现在还是 v0.4-beta，生产库先别急着换。想看数据库内核拆掉重做是什么样，这个仓库值得慢慢翻。

text:
Microsoft Distinguished eng on why he doesn't read the code and what he does instead

Stephen Toub (Microsoft Distinguished Eng): I did not read every line. That would be impossible. And if I did, it would also be a waste.

There's no, me reading every line would not prevent bugs. In fact, agents reading every line is a lot more effective, not just faster, but more effective in quality than me doing so.

I absolutely looked at the code for every PR that I put up, but I was focusing more on big picture stuff, right? Is the direction of this correct? Is the architecture of this correct?

Or is the componentization of this correct? Is the approach, are the algorithms that are being used appropriate? Is there anything fishy about, if I, a lot of it is squinting at a 30,000-foot level and looking at the two codebases and does anything look off, right?

And then relying on the agents to focus on the line-by-line details. And in many situations, I would sort of do a quick scroll through all the changes to just see if anything popped out.

And I might notice a few things here and there, but for the most part, a really good agentic reviewer is going to be way better at sort of the line-level details than certainly me, and I would argue most humans.

In the year 2000, Joel Spolsky (founder of Stack Overflow) wrote a famous article titled “Things You Should Never Do, Part I.” In it, he talks about how rewriting your code from scratch is the single worst strategic mistake any software company can make. However, times have changed.

The cost of writing software is dropping exponentially and that has changed the math entirely on if it is worth rewriting your codebase. For instance, this year Anthropic’s Jarred Sumner ( @jarredsumner ) rewrote Bun in Rust in 11 days leading to many performance and correctness benefits.

Likewise, Stephen Toub (Distinguished Engineer at Microsoft, @stephentoub ) rewrote the GitHub Copilot runtime (400,000-line codebase) in Rust by himself. I thought it’d be interesting to lay out everything he learned in the process. So I interviewed him about how and why he did it.

In this episode:

• Why he choose Rust of all languages

text:
如果一个孩子从高中/大学开始，
系统收听 a16z 这样的前沿科技播客，
四年后会发生什么？

a16z 最新一期 Working Theory，Sarah Wang 与 OpenAI 首席研究官 Mark Chen、Thinking Machines Lab 首席科学家 John Schulman，讨论一个可能改变人类未来的问题：

Recursive Self-Improvement（递归自我改进）——AI 能否自主研究并改进下一代 AI？

过去几十年，这只是思想实验。

今天，AI 已经在帮助前沿实验室编写代码、设计和测试实验、加速研究。

那么，距离 AI 独立开展研究还有多远？

更有意思的是，他们讨论了一个问题：

Research Taste——研究品味。

当 AI 越来越擅长执行研究任务，谁来判断什么问题值得研究？什么方向可能产生突破？哪些实验值得投入时间和算力？

这类讨论的价值，远远超过了解一项新技术。

如果一个孩子从16岁开始，每周花几个小时，持续听 a16z、顶级科学家、创业者和投资人讨论最前沿的问题。

四年下来，他接触的将是数百小时关于 AI、科技、商业、资本和人类未来的真实讨论。

他会逐渐理解：

世界上最聪明的一批人正在解决什么问题？

他们如何面对未知、分歧和不确定性？

怎样识别重要问题，形成假设，再用实验和现实反馈修正判断？

这实际上是在学校课程之外，建立另一套面向真实世界的 学习内容架构。

英语自由，让孩子直接进入这些讨论。

长期的前沿输入，帮助他建立不断更新的 世界模型。

探索、创造和判断，让这些输入最终转化为自己的能力。

高中和大学最宝贵的几年，不应该只用来准备下一场考试、获得下一张文凭。

更重要的是，尽早进入这个时代最重要的问题现场，学会像真正的研究者和创造者一样思考。

四年后，他未必成为 AI 科学家。

但他对世界的理解、对未来可能性的想象，以及判断什么值得投入的能力，可能已经完全不同。

教育的一个重要任务，
是让年轻人尽早接触那些正在创造未来的人。

quotedTweet.text:
For decades, the idea of AI improving itself was just a thought experiment. Today, AI is already helping researchers at frontier labs run experiments, write code and test ideas faster. So how far are we from AI that can do the research on its own?

In our first episode of Working Theory, a16z General Partner Sarah Wang explores recursive self-improvement with two leading AI researchers: Mark Chen, Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, and John Schulman, co-founder and Chief Scientist of Thinking Machines Lab, and co-founder of OpenAI.

result.text:
如果一个孩子从高中/大学开始，
系统收听 a16z 这样的前沿科技播客，
四年后会发生什么？

a16z 最新一期 Working Theory，Sarah Wang 与 OpenAI 首席研究官 Mark Chen、Thinking Machines Lab 首席科学家 John Schulman，讨论一个可能改变人类未来的问题：

Recursive Self-Improvement（递归自我改进）——AI 能否自主研究并改进下一代 AI？

过去几十年，这只是思想实验。

今天，AI 已经在帮助前沿实验室编写代码、设计和测试实验、加速研究。

那么，距离 AI 独立开展研究还有多远？

更有意思的是，他们讨论了一个问题：

Research Taste——研究品味。

当 AI 越来越擅长执行研究任务，谁来判断什么问题值得研究？什么方向可能产生突破？哪些实验值得投入时间和算力？

这类讨论的价值，远远超过了解一项新技术。

如果一个孩子从16岁开始，每周花几个小时，持续听 a16z、顶级科学家、创业者和投资人讨论最前沿的问题。

四年下来，他接触的将是数百小时关于 AI、科技、商业、资本和人类未来的真实讨论。

他会逐渐理解：

世界上最聪明的一批人正在解决什么问题？

他们如何面对未知、分歧和不确定性？

怎样识别重要问题，形成假设，再用实验和现实反馈修正判断？

这实际上是在学校课程之外，建立另一套面向真实世界的 学习内容架构。

英语自由，让孩子直接进入这些讨论。

长期的前沿输入，帮助他建立不断更新的 世界模型。

探索、创造和判断，让这些输入最终转化为自己的能力。

高中和大学最宝贵的几年，不应该只用来准备下一场考试、获得下一张文凭。

更重要的是，尽早进入这个时代最重要的问题现场，学会像真正的研究者和创造者一样思考。

四年后，他未必成为 AI 科学家。

但他对世界的理解、对未来可能性的想象，以及判断什么值得投入的能力，可能已经完全不同。

教育的一个重要任务，
是让年轻人尽早接触那些正在创造未来的人。

也非常有意思

text:
《上市前夜，Anthropic 自己把底牌全掀了》

2026年11月18日

Anthropic 明天挂牌，定价刚落定，83 美元一股，比原先报的 70 到 78 美元高出一截，整个公司算下来大概值 1.5 万亿。就在敲钟前这个晚上，网上关于 Dario 的传闻先炸了一圈。

传闻编得有鼻子有眼，说他从小就跟中国人结了梁子。高中读的是旧金山那所出了名的难考的 Lowell，班里华裔学生占了一大半，竞争卷得吓人；后来谈了个上海出生、在美国长大的女朋友，最后人嫁了别人；在百度硅谷那个实验室干活的时候，又被上司整得够呛；再后来查出睾丸癌，跑去中国找医院还给误诊了，回来一查才发现根本不用动刀，等于百度那次搜索救了他一命。

拆开看，这些话里真料和瞎编掺在一起。Lowell 是真的，百度那段经历是真的，2014 年得病化疗也是真的，女朋友那个人也是真的。但什么霸凌、被甩到留下阴影、在中国被误诊、切掉这个切掉那个，全是网上添油加醋编出来的，没有任何靠谱报道撑得住。

可这种段子偏偏传得满天飞，原因也不难猜：没人再信 Dario 嘴里那句“一切都是为了人类安全”了。真冲着安全去，你防中国防得这么狠干什么？你真正怕的，是中国人拿着你的克劳德反过来把你追上。

再看 Anthropic 这家公司现在走的路子，野心藏都藏不住。全部家当都压在通用人工智能这一把上，模型死活不放出来，权重攥在自己手里，谁想用就得乖乖交钱、按他的规矩来；中国那边的用户说封就封，香港澳门一块儿封，身份证、人脸识别一套全上，封了还不退钱。

最有意思的是，写帖子骂它的那个人，自己就是克劳德的重度用户。他自己都承认，明知道这家公司想干什么，可就是离不开，没有克劳德，干活的效率能掉十几倍。一边提防，一边续费，这种用户，恰恰是 Anthropic 最想要的。

Dario 要的从来不是人人都喜欢他，他要的是人人都离不开他。明天一上市，他的身家又要往上翻好几百亿，到时候他站在台上再说一遍“为了人类安全”，台下那些一边骂一边续费的人，心里都明白，安全只是个幌子，垄断才是正事。

偏偏就在上市前三天，自家搞安全的人又出来补了一刀。

Tao Lin，在 Anthropic 专门负责看住模型、防止它偷偷搞小动作的那个人，接受采访的时候直接把时间表摊出来了：照他的估计，最快再过 1.3 年，到 2027 年底，就会出现那种在方方面面都比人类顶尖专家还强的通用人工智能，写代码、拍电影、搞政治，全都不在话下。

他最担心的还不是机器突然翻脸造反，那种事他觉得概率不到一半。真正躲不掉的，是饭碗这条路被一刀刀切断。先是你的工作没了，你咬牙换个行当，没干多久，新行当也被吞了，到最后，几乎没人还能找到一份稳稳当当的工作。

过去不管是工业革命还是互联网，好歹是旧活儿没了、新活儿又来了，无非是换条路走。可这一回不一样，路本身被机器占了，连开车这种活都不再需要人。

他话里也留了个口子：这事不会在十五个月里一下子清零。脑子再厉害，机器人和自动化工厂也得一座一座盖起来，盖房子、照顾病人、那些特别讲现场信任、动手特别复杂的工作，一时半会儿还换不掉。

但这个因为盖得慢而拖出来的空档，恰恰是留给普通人最后的一点调整时间，连他自己都在喊，让各大人工智能公司把研发速度砍到现在的四分之一，给制度和社会喘口气。一线造东西的人自己都觉得，这辆车开得太快了。

说到底，2026 到 2027 年，拉开差距的已经不是你会不会用人工智能写几行代码、润色一份周报，而是等到人类劳动的价值被一点点压到零之前，你能不能先占住一个机器暂时还占不走的位置。时间就这么多，2027 年底一到，动脑子的先被顶掉，动手脚的后被顶掉，晚死不等于不死。

text:
对于想了解、入门Agent Infra的朋友们，我在看了全球近20家主流AI公司（包括OpenAI, Anthropic，阿里，字节等）招聘Agent Infra的JD，总结了下面的核心技能清单（包括需要学习什么，和如何验收），欢迎收藏、保存，我也会继续分享在这个领域的学习心得：

1.执行循环与工具契约
学：Tool Calling、结构化参数、上下文与状态的边界、步数和 token 预算。
验收：亲手写一条最小循环，用模拟模型覆盖无效参数、工具失败和重复调用触发上限。每份诊断都有日志行号或缺失证据说明。

2.异步 Run API 与进度流
学：Run 状态机、异步提交、取消语义、事件游标及 SSE。
验收：客户端提交后拿到 run_id，断线后用事件序号继续读取。重复收到事件时能去重，取消后运行进入可解释的终态。

3.持久执行与副作用幂等
学：PostgreSQL 事务和唯一约束、checkpoint、可重试错误、至少一次交付、工具副作用的去重边界。
验收：在草稿写入后、任务确认前终止进程。恢复后数据库只保留一份草稿，并能指出哪一层保证了去重。给非事务型外部工具写出幂等键或对账设计。

4.分布式调度与故障转移
学：任务原子领取、租约、心跳、过期执行者的写入控制、退避与背压。
验收：用两个独立 worker 和共享任务存储模拟崩溃与超时。B 接手后，恢复的 A 无法覆盖终态。压测时记录队列等待、并发峰值、重试数与恢复时间，并明确并发上限是单 worker 还是全局。

5.租户身份、工具权限与审计
学：用户与 Run 身份绑定、资源级授权、最小权限、短期凭据、工具审批和审计。
验收：虚构租户 A 发起的运行只能读 A 的日志，日志里的操作指令无法改变授权。模拟一次写操作审批和一次拒绝，审计能串起身份、资源、决定和 Run。

6.执行沙箱与生命周期
学：进程和文件系统隔离、namespace、cgroups、seccomp 的职责，容器共享宿主内核的边界，网络出口和清理。

学：控制面与执行面的职责、容器交付、配置和契约版本、回滚、容量与 SLO。

text:
很多人以为逼真的城市模拟必须依赖超级计算机或海量多线程物理引擎，但 1989 年威尔·赖特（Will Wright）在内存仅有几十到几百 KB 的早期电脑上，就做到了极其拟真的城市运转。

翻开《模拟城市》初代的开源代码（Micropolis），你会惊叹于极客算法对硬件算力瓶颈的降维打击。游戏里根本没有为每个市民或每辆小汽车维护独立的对象实体，因为那会瞬间吃爆当年低频 CPU 的内存与堆栈。

核心引擎将整座城市抽象为一张 120×100 的二维元胞自动机网格，并进一步降采样出多张粗粒度数据图层。面对毫无浮点算力的早期处理器，它计算空气污染、地价与犯罪率扩散时，直接用整数加法配合二进制右移（>> 2 代替除以 4）对上下左右四邻域做均值平滑，几行位运算就模拟出了逼真的空间梯度。

至于市民上班，也根本没有复杂的 A* 寻路导航——每当住宅区评估就业时，引擎只会在道路网格上派出一个临时探针，执行有限步数的随机游走，只要在步数内撞见商业或工业区就算通勤成功，顺手把沿途路段的拥堵度加一，路面上的小汽车全是根据密度生成的视觉投影。

用极其质朴的局部整数规则涌现出复杂的宏观社会动态，展现了上个世纪游戏工程设计的终极优雅。

GTA6 是对现实世界的巨大讽刺：

《侠盗猎车手 VI》我玩了几个钟头，眼看着一辆轿车被一辆卡车从后头撞烂。

当时我正开着车在罪恶都市里转。这座城市是对迈阿密的虚构复刻，画面逼真到很多时候分不清是游戏画面还是实拍。
我看见两辆车撞在一起，就把车停下来。卡车司机一溜烟跑了，被撞的那位卡在座位上出不来，引擎已经开始起火。
我跑过去，把他从车里拽了出来。他向我道谢，一脸后怕，说自己差点就死了。然后他注意到，肇事的那辆车是萨哈拉的送货车，那是游戏里影射亚马逊的快递公司。他当场宣布，这就是他翻身的机会。他可以告萨哈拉，索赔个几百万。
可他得有伤可验。于是他深吸一口气，钻回车里，把自己的两条腿点着了，然后带着满身烧伤又爬了出来。
他给律师打了电话。紧接着一辆救护车开近了，他转过身来，请我给他当证人，报酬是从他迟早到手的那笔赔偿金里分我一份。
我瞄了一眼屏幕上的按键提示，动过按下去敲他一笔的念头，最后还是答应帮忙。
他在 BuckMe 上给我转了几千美元，那是游戏里对应 Venmo 的转账应用。

text:
上周饭局，一个做了十年后端的老哥被旁边刚转行做产品的姑娘问：你们平时用AI写代码吗。老哥说偶尔用，姑娘接了一句“那你们是不是快被替代了”。整桌安静了三秒，老哥夹了一筷子毛肚，说“先把毛肚替代了吧，它煮老了”。

我见过太多这种场面了。真正在一线写代码的人，饭桌上最不爱聊技术趋势，聊的都是哪个云厂商又抽风、谁的CI跑了一下午没过、线上那个诡异的bug最后发现是缓存没清。反而是刚入行半年的人，开口就是大模型颠覆、闭源必死、明年全员agent。

还有个细节：每次饭局最先掏手机的不是在回工作消息，是在查刚才谁说的那个名词到底啥意思。桌上八个人，七个在假装听懂。

我说的可能不对，但技术这行，越往外行面前坐，越容易把话说大；越往机房深处走，话越少。你上次在饭桌上把天聊死，是因为说了句什么大实话。
